transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-22 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Moran (Redwood AE), Priya Sethi (Redwood SE), Jonah Lee (Redwood Product), Marta Ruiz (Aperture Head of ML), Ethan Park (Platform Eng), Sofia Nair (Finance), Ryan Cole (CTO)

Summary: Short demo of the Redwood Console Insights pages focusing on per-route dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns, and Optimize suggestions. Customer asked about token attribution, multi-route mapping, and how to reconcile console numbers with their internal billing. Agreed to run a POC bench and share exports and sample dashboards.

[00:00] Alex Moran: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we'll give a quick run through the console insights pages, show per-route cost, and then dig into Optimize suggestions for batching and kv cache. If you have questions interrupt anytime.
[00:22] Marta Ruiz: Sounds good, we just want to see how we'd split costs between product lines and prove out savings before committing to dedicated.
[00:30] Priya Sethi: Great, I'll drive the demo. First, dashboard landing — you can see top-level metrics: total tokens, average latency p50/p95, and cost estimate by token and embedding units.
[00:48] Priya Sethi: (narrating) Here is the 'Routes' tab — each route maps to an API route or function you define. You can group by tag if you prefer product-line mapping. See how we show token counts per route and cost burned per model variant.
[01:10] Ethan Park: Is that per-tenant? We have a multi-tenant service, will we be able to split by customer + route?
[01:16] Priya Sethi: Yes, you can dimension by tenant id if you send that metadata in the request. We support per-token attribution using the metadata header — it's what a lot of platform teams do.
[01:29] Marta Ruiz: How accurate is the cost estimate — we saw differences when comparing to our infra invoices.
[01:36] Alex Moran: Good question. Console shows token-level charge estimates using our current unit rates and embedding multipliers. It intentionally matches the hosted billing model but excludes infra overhead when you're on private/dedicated. There are two reconcile sources: token accounting (console) and infra spend (cloud bill).
[01:53] Priya Sethi: Also, note caching and batching change token counts. Console exposes an effective tokens metric (after prefix cache hits and reranker short-circuits). That can look lower than raw tokens your app logs.
[02:12] Jonah Lee: Example: we had a customer where prefix KV cache removed 18% of generation tokens during peak, so their console cost dropped by that percentage even though request counts stayed the same.
[02:28] Ryan Cole: Walk us through the per-route drilldown please.
[02:32] Priya Sethi: Sure — click into a route. Top section: traffic chart by hour, model variant breakdown, p50/p95 latency. Middle: cost waterfall — token cost, model variant multipliers (e.g., embedding calls), and batching efficiency. Bottom: Optimize suggestions — quantization recommendation, batching window, and cache TTL suggestions.
[02:57] [03:00] Marta Ruiz: Can we export this data? Our finance team will want a CSV with the same breakdown.
[03:05] Alex Moran: Yes, there's an export button. We can do per-route exports scoped by date range. We'll include token-level columns: prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, cache_hits, effective_tokens, model, cost_estimate_usd.
[03:23] Ethan Park: What about attribution when a single front end call fans out to several routes? Like frontend->llm->reranker->embedding. How do you attribute cost?
[03:34] Priya Sethi: We have a route graph mode — you can define an execution trace id and Redwood will attribute costs along the chain. By default we report the immediate route that invoked the model, but with trace ids you get end-to-end attribution.
[03:50] Marta Ruiz: Do we need to change our SDK for that?
[03:52] Priya Sethi: Minimal, you add a trace header and route name on each internal call. We can give you a small snippet.
[04:02] [04:10] Sofia Nair: On the cost waterfall: are embeddings billed differently? We run a lot of embedding lookups and want to separate those.
[04:16] Priya Sethi: Embeddings show as a separate line item with per-embed unit cost and vector-store ops highlighted. You can filter the console to show 'embeddings only' and see top queries by cost.
[04:28] Alex Moran: Also worth noting: Optimize will detect hot queries that could be cached as static embeddings and propose moving them to a product cache. That often reduces embedding spend by 60-80% for search-heavy apps.
[04:44] [05:00] Customer interruption / cross talk
[05:10] Marta Ruiz: Are there built-in alerts for cost spikes? We need to know before the bill arrives.
[05:15] Priya Sethi: Yes — you can set threshold alerts on total cost burn rate, per-route spend delta, or anomalies detected by our time-series model. Alerts push to Slack, PagerDuty, or email.
[05:29] Ethan Park: Can rules auto-block a route if it exceeds a budget?
[05:33] Alex Moran: You can create enforcement policies: soft limits (alert + throttle) or hard limits (reject calls). For production we recommend a soft limit plus a canary fallback model to preserve UX.
[05:50] [06:00] Jonah Lee: Quick note on how batching affects latency/cost tradeoffs — Console's Optimize tab will suggest batching window sizes based on your latency SLO and observed inter-arrival times.
[06:12] Marta Ruiz: Show us an example.
[06:15] Priya Sethi: (navigates) Here's a sample route where we recommend a 12ms batching window — that gave 25% token cost reduction with sub-10ms added latency at p95. We also surface the expected reduction in inferred $/1M tokens.
[06:34] Ryan Cole: Are these simulated numbers or from live runs?
[06:36] Priya Sethi: They come from both: we simulate using your traffic distribution and and then validate during a short bench if you enable the POC. The recommendation page shows confidence and sample size.
[06:50] [07:00] Sofia Nair: About reconciliation — if we run a POC, how will you make sure your console numbers match our Azure bill?
[07:09] Alex Moran: For POC we'll send a run plan. We'll include token export and kernel/runtime logs for inference runtime. On dedicated/private there will be infra costs to add; we'll give an itemized estimate.
[07:24] Marta Ruiz: One of our concerns is double counting when we do server-side batching plus client aggregation.
[07:30] Priya Sethi: Console shows both raw incoming tokens and effective tokens after server-side batching and cache hits. You can toggle to see raw vs effective to spot double counting.
[07:42] [08:00] Ethan Park: Could you show the Optimize rule editor? We want to create a rule that says: for route X, if p95 latency > 800ms then shift traffic to smaller local model and alert.
[08:10] Priya Sethi: (clicks into editor) Here's the rule builder. Condition: metric p95 latency > 800ms. Action: reroute to fallback-model-v2 (smaller) + Slack notify finance and ops. You can add cooldown windows.
[08:27] Marta Ruiz: Nice — and you can also do A/B rollouts?
[08:30] Priya Sethi: Yep, canary % rollouts, weighted A/B, and automatic rollback on quality regressions if you feed eval sets.
[08:39] [09:00] Alex Moran: For your finance team specifically, the per-route export will include the model version, token counts, caching stats, and cost_estimate_usd. That should map to the token lines in your sheet. We'll add a reconciliation guide.
[09:15] Sofia Nair: Great — also, can we tag spend to product lines? Eg route tags -> GL code?
[09:21] Priya Sethi: Yes, you can add arbitrary tags to routes. Then the Console lets you group by tag and export grouped totals.
[09:30] Marta Ruiz: One security question — who can see cost data? We have separate finance and infra teams, and we need RBAC.
[09:36] Alex Moran: Console supports RBAC by role. You can restrict routes, data visibility, and export permissions. SSO via SAML/Okta and audit logs are available for Private/Enterprise plans.
[09:50] [10:00] Ethan Park: A couple of nitty gritty: does the console backfill if we enable tracing mid-month?
[10:07] Priya Sethi: We keep raw token logs for 90 days (configurable). If you turn tracing on mid-month, we'll show data from that point forward; we can do a one-time ingest of historical logs if you share them with us.
[10:22] Marta Ruiz: Can you show the SVG export for charts? Our product reports like PNG.
[10:27] Priya Sethi: Charts can be exported as CSV/PNG/SVG.
[10:30] [11:00] (Priya navigates to a saved dashboard)
[11:05] Priya Sethi: Here's a saved dashboard for a hypothetical SaaS customer with routes grouped by product vertical. Notice the heatmap for per-route cost per 1000 requests. The right column shows Optimize recommendations and a projected monthly spend baseline.
[11:22] Ryan Cole: What's the projected time to set this up for us — we have about ten routes to instrument.
[11:28] Alex Moran: Basic instrumentation is minutes to hours — most of our customers get the first dashboard in under a day. Full attribution and tagging for 10 routes usually takes a few days with the SDK snippets and a short ops window.
[11:43] Marta Ruiz: For the POC bench we want to run two scenarios: current config and Redwood recommended (batching+cache). Can you run both and produce side-by-side cost/latency?
[11:53] Priya Sethi: Yes — that's exactly what the POC bench does. We'll capture p50/p95 latency, throughput, token counts, and cost estimates and give you a side-by-side report.
[12:05] [12:30] Customer questions / clarifying details
[12:42] Alex Moran: Quick recap: we'll send the per-route export + sample dashboard; Priya will schedule the POC bench and share the run plan; Ethan will provide traffic samples; Sofia will send current cost spreadsheet. Any blockers?
[12:55] Marta Ruiz: No blockers from our side. We'll aim to get finance and platform aligned this week.
[13:03] Alex Moran: Great, I'll follow up with links and the export by Friday. Thanks everyone.

Meeting end.

References mentioned: 1) Sample dashboard link (shared post-call) 2) POC run plan doc (will be shared) 3) Per-route export CSV (will be attached)

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker mislabels and punctuation gaps.
